matchstick.title: Compute numeric values and discrepancy
matchstick.principle: Convert each Roman numeral in the equation to its integer value and compute the difference between the left‑hand side total and the right‑hand side total. This difference tells you how much the equation must be increased or decreased.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving, before generating stick‑move candidates.
matchstick.example: Attempting stick moves without first calculating that XIII (13) and VI+II (8) differ by 5.

matchstick.title: List possible single‑stick transformations
matchstick.principle: Generate every way a single matchstick can be removed from one character and added to another (or repositioned) while keeping each character a valid Roman numeral or operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After knowing the required numeric change, to create a list of candidate moves.
matchstick.example: Listing moves that take a stick from V and discard V, forgetting that V cannot lose a stick and stay valid.

matchstick.title: Match numeric difference to value change
matchstick.principle: For each candidate move, compute how the values of the affected numerals change and check whether the net change equals the previously computed discrepancy.
matchstick.example: Choosing a move that changes VI to VII (+1) when the needed change is +5, resulting in a still‑incorrect equation.

matchstick.title: Operator modification via plus
matchstick.principle: A ‘+’ consists of one vertical and one horizontal stick; removing the vertical stick turns it into ‘‑’, and removing the horizontal stick turns it into ‘I’. Adding a missing stick can reverse these changes.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the required numeric adjustment can be achieved by flipping a plus into a minus (or vice versa).
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical stick from ‘+’ but forgetting to change the addition to subtraction, leaving the sum unchanged.

matchstick.title: Operator‑to‑numeral stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If adding a stick from an operator to a numeral yields exactly the needed value change, move that stick from the operator to the numeral, ensuring the operator remains a valid symbol after losing the stick.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric gap matches a known increment that can be supplied by a stick from a plus or minus sign.
matchstick.example: Moving the horizontal stick from ‘+’ to a numeral but leaving the operator as a lone vertical line, which is not a valid operator.

matchstick.title: Equation structure preservation
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, the equation must still contain exactly one ‘=’, at least one valid numeral on each side, and only the allowed operators (+, -).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after any candidate move, before checking numeric equality.
matchstick.example: Dropping the ‘=’ sign or turning it into a non‑equal symbol, producing an ill‑formed equation.

matchstick.title: Known single‑stick numeral transformations
matchstick.principle: Use a lookup of common one‑stick numeral changes (e.g., I→II (+1), I→IV (+3), V↔X (+5), I↔V (+4)) to quickly identify which numerals can be altered to achieve a specific value change.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When matching the required numeric change to a known transformation.
matchstick.example: Missing the V↔X (+5) transformation and only trying I‑based changes, thus failing to find the correct move.

matchstick.title: Operator sign change impact
matchstick.principle: If a stick move changes an operator (e.g., ‘+’ to ‘‑’), recompute the affected term using the new sign before testing the equality.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a candidate move modifies an operator.
matchstick.example: Changing ‘+’ to ‘‑’ but still adding the second operand, leading to an incorrect total.

matchstick.title: Single‑stick relocation constraint
matchstick.principle: A move must involve exactly one individual stick; you cannot remove an entire character or add a new stick beyond the one being moved.
matchstick.example: Attempting to delete the whole ‘V’ and replace it with an ‘X’, which uses more than one stick.

matchstick.title: Intra‑character stick reposition allowed
matchstick.principle: When a single‑stick transformation changes a character’s shape (e.g., V↔X) without adding or removing sticks from other characters, treat it as moving the stick within the same character; only the final character must be a valid numeral/operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the needed numeric change matches a known intra‑character transformation and no other character can supply a stick, consider repositioning a stick inside that character.
matchstick.example: Rejecting V→X because V cannot lose a stick, instead of repositioning a diagonal stick within V to form X.

matchstick.description: Leaving a character invalid after moving a stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes the source character must stay valid after losing a stick, causing it to discard moves that actually involve repositioning within the same character.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Allow moves that change a character’s shape by repositioning a stick inside it (e.g., V↔X); only the final shape must be valid.

matchstick.description: Failing to verify numeric equality after transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model stops after making a syntactically valid change without recomputing the arithmetic result.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always recompute the left‑hand and right‑hand totals after any stick move and confirm they are equal before output.

matchstick.description: Dropping or omitting parts of the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model truncates the expression when focusing on a local change, forgetting to include all original symbols.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure the final answer contains the full equation with exactly one ‘=’ and all original numerals/operators (except those altered by the stick move).

matchstick.description: Ignoring the numeric impact of operator sign change
matchstick.why_it_happens: When changing ‘+’ to ‘‑’, the model does not adjust the arithmetic sign of the affected term.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Recalculate the expression using the new operator sign before checking equality.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes adds or removes more than one stick, or treats a whole character as a single stick.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Count sticks explicitly; only one stick may be taken from one character and placed onto another (or repositioned within the same character).
